strings.d1.theme: Izmir's iconic face: Kordon, Kemeraltı, Konak
strings.d1.s0.name: Clock Tower and Konak Square
strings.d1.s0.tips: The 1901 clock tower is Izmir's official symbol, and early morning is the best time to photograph it without crowds. Before you start your day, stop for simit (sesame bread ring) and tea by the Konak Ferry Pier on the square.
strings.d1.s1.name: Kemeraltı Bazaar (Anafartalar Street)
strings.d1.s1.tips: Get lost in the narrow lanes around the spice sellers, jewellers and Kızlarağası Han; every corner has a different trader. In summer heat, fresh apricots and dried fruit from the stalls make a cheap, easy snack.
strings.d1.s2.name: Kemeraltı Bazaar Food Tour
strings.d1.s2.tips: The guided tasting tour follows a food route of 6-7 stops, with boyoz (Izmir's baked pastry), kokoreç (seasoned grilled offal), baklava and Turkish coffee. It takes you to trader shops you would not find on your own. Book online at least 1 day ahead and come hungry.
strings.d1.s3.name: Kültürpark
strings.d1.s3.tips: In the city park dating from 1936 you can rent a rowing boat on the pond (100-150 TL). The tree-lined areas are ideal for escaping the afternoon heat. The fairground may close in September for the Izmir International Fair; outside that period it is quiet.
strings.d1.s4.name: Kordon (Cumhuriyet Boulevard) Sunset Walk
strings.d1.s4.tips: Watch the sunset over the bay from near Alsancak Pier; the palm-lined promenade is busy with local cyclists and joggers. Turkish coffee from the roaming vendors costs around 100-150 TL, and you won't need to look for a bench.
strings.d1.s5.name: Deniz Restaurant
strings.d1.s5.tips: A classic fish restaurant in the Izmir Palas Hotel, serving for over 30 years, with views right onto the Kordon. Ask about the seasonal meze and the catch of the day. For garden tables on summer evenings, booking is recommended (0232 464 4499).
strings.d1.b0.name: Historic Güven Restaurant
strings.d1.b0.tips: A tradesmen's restaurant open since 1939 in Kemeraltı, lunchtime only. Try the tripe with chickpeas and the kuru fasulye (white bean stew); after 13:00 there may be a queue.
strings.d1.b1.name: Hisar Mosque
strings.d1.b1.tips: Built in 1597, this is Izmir's largest and oldest mosque, right next to Kızlarağası Han. With its single-balcony minaret and six small domes, it makes a short stop on a Kemeraltı walk.
strings.d2.theme: Layers of history: Havra, Agora, Kadifekale
strings.d2.s0.name: Agora Open Air Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: Wander among the surviving columns of the Roman-era ancient marketplace; it is not crowded at the 08:30 opening. Museum Pass is valid. There is little shade, so going early is a must.
strings.d2.s1.name: Havra Street Synagogues (Bikur Holim and Algazi Synagogue)
strings.d2.s1.tips: The locked synagogues of a 500-year-old Sephardic heritage can only be visited with special permission. Call Ebruli Turizm at least 2-3 days ahead to book a place on the Havra Street tour. The meeting point is Mezarlıkbaşı, at the entrance of 927 Sokak.
strings.d2.s2.name: Bizim Restaurant
strings.d2.s2.tips: A family business of 39 years, famous for its tripe with chickpeas and fish soup. Fish soup is served Tuesday to Friday, and paça çorbası (trotter soup) on Wednesday. It stands on 911 Sokak, parallel to Kızlarağası Han, a plain tradesmen's restaurant that looks almost signless.
strings.d2.s3.name: Kızlarağası Han
strings.d2.s3.tips: The courtyard of this 18th-century caravanserai holds antique dealers, handicraft shops and nargile cafés. Stopping at the courtyard tea garden and chatting with the traders is the best part of the tour.
strings.d2.s4.name: Kadifekale Sunset View
strings.d2.s4.tips: From the city's highest point the whole bay turns red. Arrive 45 minutes before sunset; the blue hour (20-30 minutes after sunset) gives the most dramatic light. Get tea from the roaming tea sellers at the foot of the walls.
strings.d2.s5.name: Park Pide Salonu
strings.d2.s5.tips: In the Güven neighbourhood at the foot of Kadifekale, this is a plain pide (Turkish flatbread boat) place that locals use. Try the kaşarlı (cheese) or kıymalı (minced meat) pide with ayran; in the evenings local families fill it.
strings.d2.b0.name: Kısmet Restaurant
strings.d2.b0.tips: A tradesmen's restaurant inside Küçük Demirhan in Kemeraltı, serving for over 40 years. Pick whatever you like from the daily pot dishes at the counter; prices are close to Bizim Restaurant.
strings.d2.b1.name: YOLO (Abacıoğlu Han)
strings.d2.b1.tips: An alternative venue in one of Kemeraltı's hans, with constantly changing exhibitions and vintage items upstairs. You can also take a break with imported beer and homemade burgers.
strings.d3.theme: Alsancak's soul: boyoz, art, stone houses
strings.d3.s0.name: Zeynel Ergin Gevrek Bakery
strings.d3.s0.tips: This bakery on 1466 Sokak is Izmir's gevrek (simit) symbol, baking fresh since 06:30. Don't forget the boyoz, which comes in chocolate and cheese varieties and is served warm if you go early in the morning.
strings.d3.s1.name: Alsancak Punta Historic Houses
strings.d3.s1.tips: In the area known as 'La Punta' in the Ottoman era, there are colourful-fronted consulate and mansion buildings from the 19th century. It is a quiet photo route that tourist crowds don't reach.
strings.d3.s2.name: Arkas Art Center
strings.d3.s2.tips: A free art gallery in the former French consulate building from the early 1900s, with 9 exhibition halls. Closed on Monday; easily seen in 1-2 hours.
strings.d3.s3.name: Kumru and Stuffed Mussels Break in Alsancak
strings.d3.s3.tips: Try kumru (toasted sausage-and-cheese sandwich) and midye dolma (stuffed mussels) from the stands around Kıbrıs Şehitleri Street. It is a lunchtime favourite of Izmir locals, quick and cheap on the go. Ayran or şalgam (spiced turnip juice) goes with it.
strings.d3.s4.name: Side Streets off Kıbrıs Şehitleri Street
strings.d3.s4.tips: On streets 1461-1465 behind the main avenue, old Alsancak buildings, boutique shops and small cafés are tucked away. They are not marked on Google Maps, so this route is left to your own discovery.
strings.d3.s5.name: Yasef's Tavern
strings.d3.s5.tips: A friendly place reopened by the grandchild of a historic tavern that closed 80 years ago. Expect lively conversation over Aegean meze and rakı; book ahead for the weekend.
strings.d3.b0.name: Dostlar Bakery
strings.d3.b0.tips: Another legendary boyoz baker in Alsancak, known for its chocolate, tahini and lentil varieties. An alternative to Zeynel Ergin, ideal for a morning breakfast.
strings.d3.b1.name: Gündoğdu Square
strings.d3.b1.tips: One of Alsancak's liveliest squares, known for its equestrian statue of Atatürk. There are benches around it for sitting and people-watching. Worth a stop in the late afternoon to cool off.
strings.d4.theme: Across the bay: Karşıyaka and Bostanlı
strings.d4.s0.name: Konak-Karşıyaka Ferry and Karşıyaka Bazaar
strings.d4.s0.tips: The 25-minute ferry ride from Konak Pier costs 35 TL with the Izmirim Kart and is the best way to see the bay from above. In the bazaar opposite Karşıyaka Pier, wander among bookshops and cafés.
strings.d4.s1.name: National Struggle Park and Museum (Latife Hanım Mansion)
strings.d4.s1.tips: The mansion where Atatürk's mother Zübeyde Hanım spent her last days displays objects from the War of Independence era. It is Karşıyaka's most overlooked historic stop and is usually quiet.
strings.d4.s2.name: Köfteci Erol
strings.d4.s2.tips: One of the district's oldest köfte (grilled meatball) restaurants, with a casual décor inside Karşıyaka Bazaar. Order it with piyaz (white bean salad) and a frothy ayran; at lunchtime it is full of regulars.
strings.d4.s3.name: Bostanlı Market
strings.d4.s3.tips: Held on Wednesdays and Saturdays, this market offers everything from organic produce to homemade jam. Chat with local producers and pick up a small souvenir.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bostanlı Waterfront and Cycle Path
strings.d4.s4.tips: On the long bike and walking path with bay views, you can take a pleasant ride on a rented bike (around 150 TL). Late afternoon is the busiest time, when Izmir locals exercise.
strings.d4.s5.name: Bostanlı Sunset Viewing Terrace and Kumrucu Ömür
strings.d4.s5.tips: After watching the sunset from the terrace stretching out toward the sea, have dinner nearby at Kumrucu Ömür, Bostanlı's best kumru place. A full kumru and ayran is the classic combination.
strings.d4.b0.name: Kumrucu Şevki
strings.d4.b0.tips: One of Karşıyaka's best-known kumru places, practical as it is open at all hours. A full kumru with ayran is the standard.
strings.d4.b1.name: Bostanlı Ferry Pier
strings.d4.b1.tips: Karşıyaka's other pier is an alternative sunset spot to the waterfront terrace. You can chat with the fishermen around the pier.
strings.d5.s0.name: Balçova Thermal Facilities (Agamemnon Hot Springs)
strings.d5.s0.tips: Day-use pool entry to the thermal waters, used since antiquity, is around 75-100 TL. Last entry is 17:00, so go early in the morning for an unhurried spa experience.
strings.d5.s1.name: Inciraltı Urban Forest
strings.d5.s1.tips: A city forest with wide green spaces and walking paths, where families picnic and tourists almost never go. You can shelter from the midday heat in the shaded areas.
strings.d5.s2.name: Güzelbahçe Fishing Shelter
strings.d5.s2.tips: With its small boats and nets, this is one of the Aegean's most genuine corners; the shelter comes alive when fishermen return from the morning catch. It is the quietest and most authentic spot for photos.
strings.d5.s3.name: Lunch in Güzelbahçe
strings.d5.s3.tips: Ask for the fresh catch of the day at a small fish restaurant near the fishing shelter; prices are lower than on the Kordon. A quiet spot that locals favour at weekends.
strings.d5.s4.name: Güzelbahçe Seafront Walk and Cycling
strings.d5.s4.tips: You can rent a bike along the quiet shoreline, and there are spots where you can swim. This is a beach away from the Kordon crowds, preferred by locals.
strings.d5.s5.name: Sunset and Fish Sandwich on Narlıdere Seafront
strings.d5.s5.tips: On the way back, watch the sunset on Narlıdere seafront and eat a balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from a boat stall. It is one of the most authentic and cheapest dinner options. Ayran or şalgam goes with it.
strings.d5.b0.name: Balçova Thermal Hotel Restaurant
strings.d5.b0.tips: The restaurant inside the thermal complex is a practical lunch option after the spa. Its menu is mostly regional home cooking.
strings.d5.b1.name: Izmir Balçova Cable Car
strings.d5.b1.tips: The cable car from Balçova to Şirinyer gives you a bird's-eye view of the city; the fare is 80 TL. In summer, closing time is extended to 20:00.
strings.d6.s0.name: Ephesus
strings.d6.s0.tips: One of the world's best-preserved ancient cities; don't miss the Library of Celsus and the Great Theatre. The tour price includes transport, guiding and site entry. Go early to avoid the heat.
strings.d6.s1.name: House of the Virgin Mary
strings.d6.s1.tips: This small stone house, believed by Christians to be where the Virgin Mary spent her last years, is sacred to Christian and Muslim visitors alike. You can leave a wish on the wishing wall.
strings.d6.s2.name: Lunch in Selçuk
strings.d6.s2.tips: Try the local köfte at Selçuk Köftecisi (Şehabettin Dede Street), a practical stop near the bus station after the Ephesus tour. Ödemiş köfte with kaymak (clotted cream) is the region's speciality.
strings.d6.s3.name: Şirince Village Stone Streets
strings.d6.s3.tips: Get lost among the stone houses of Greek architecture and the narrow streets; wine tasting in the cellars is completely free. To escape the crowds, turn into the back streets off the main road.
strings.d6.s4.name: Local Wine and Jam Shopping in Şirince
strings.d6.s4.tips: Taste a few of the pomegranate, strawberry and black mulberry wines and buy what you like. The organic jam and olive oil that villagers make at home are also a must-try. There is room to bargain when paying cash.
strings.d6.b0.name: Ayasuluk Castle and Isa Bey Mosque
strings.d6.b0.tips: As an alternative to Ephesus, this castle on top of Selçuk also holds the ruins of the Basilica of St. John. Museum Pass is valid; closing time is 17:30.
strings.d6.b1.name: Selçuk Köftecisi
strings.d6.b1.tips: Opposite the bus station, this is a köfte place favoured by locals; a plain, quick alternative to the main restaurant.
strings.d7.theme: Alaçatı and Çeşme: stone lanes, sea
strings.d7.s0.name: Alaçatı Stone Streets and Windmills
strings.d7.s0.tips: The 150-year-old windmills at the entrance to Alaçatı look their most photogenic in daylight; right after, walk the stone streets with colourful doors. Get there with the Izmirim Kart on ESHOT lines 984-760.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pazaryeri Mosque (Ayios Konstantinos Church)
strings.d7.s1.tips: Built as a church in 1874 and later turned into a mosque, this is an intriguing building and a symbol of different faiths intertwined. It is rarely mentioned on Alaçatı's tourist routes.
strings.d7.s2.name: Kumrucu Hüseyin
strings.d7.s2.tips: Master Hüseyin, the inventor of the kumru, has been in the same spot since 1966 and at 85 is still running the shop. Order a full kumru; it is Çeşme's most authentic food stop.
strings.d7.s3.name: Sea Day at Ilıca Beach
strings.d7.s3.tips: A free public beach at the entrance to Çeşme, with shallow, clear water that families like too. If you want to rent a sunlounger, expect an extra fee of around 150-250 TL.
strings.d7.b0.name: Kumrucu Erol
strings.d7.b0.tips: A family business since the 1980s, this is another historic kumru place and an alternative to Kumrucu Hüseyin. It is also a local favourite.
strings.d7.b1.name: Çeşme Castle
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Genoese-era castle offers a short history break before heading back, as an alternative to Ilıca. The museum inside displays objects on the history of piracy and seafaring.
strings.note0: You can't board any public transport (bus, metro, ferry) without an Izmirim Kart. Without one you can only board with a contactless bank card, at a slightly higher fare.
strings.note1: In July, midday temperatures reach 34-38°C, so avoid long walks between 12:00 and 16:00. The imbat (sea breeze) feels cool, but the sun still burns, so a hat and sunscreen are essential.
strings.note2: For the synagogue visit on Havra Street, wear clothes that cover shoulders and knees; men are given a kippa at the door. Ask your guide before taking photos.
strings.note3: Tipping is not required at tradesmen's restaurants (Bizim Restaurant, Güven Restaurant). At more modern restaurants (Deniz Restaurant, Yasef's Tavern), leaving 10% is customary if it isn't included in the bill.
strings.note4: Set out on day trips such as Ephesus and Alaçatı in the first hours if you can (08:00-09:00); you avoid both the summer heat and the tour-bus crowds.
strings.note5: The narrow lanes of Kemeraltı Bazaar get busier especially in the afternoon, so carry your bag in front of you.
strings.note6: Bargaining for wine or jam from local producers in Şirince and Alaçatı isn't considered rude, and you can ask for a discount on bulk purchases.
strings.niche.name: Havra Street Synagogues (Bikur Holim and Algazi Synagogue)
strings.niche.why_hidden: Most guidebooks describe Kemeraltı's spice scent and colourful stalls but skip the 500-year-old Sephardic heritage right behind it. Because Izmir's Jewish community has shrunk, the synagogues are closed to daily worship and can only be visited with special permission, by prior appointment.
strings.niche.access_instructions: Call Ebruli Turizm at least 2-3 days ahead to book the Havra Street tour (including the Shalom, Algazi, Bikur Holim and restored Etz Hayim synagogues). The group meets in the Mezarlıkbaşı neighbourhood, at the Kemeraltı entrance of 927 Sokak.
strings.niche.insider_tip: Men are given a kippa at the door; wear clothes that cover shoulders and knees. Ask your guide to show old photographs of Kemeraltı from the 19th-century 'Cadde-i Kebir' era, which standard tours don't cover.
strings.niche.season: Possible all year, but extra events and concerts are held during the Sephardic Culture Festival in spring.
strings.transit.name: Izmirim Kart
strings.transit.why_chosen: In Izmir the metro, tram, IZBAN, all ESHOT buses (including lines 984-760 to Alaçatı) and IZDENIZ ferries (including the Konak-Karşıyaka route) all run on this one card. Nearly every day of your plan needs at least one public transport connection. It is cheaper than single tickets and practical, with top-up machines at every station.
